sections.headline: Nasdaq Rebounds from AI Stock Sell-Off

sections.headline: Yield Hike Sparks Market Concerns

sections.headline: USD/JPY Rises on Yen Strength
sections.body: The USD/JPY pair rose as traders took advantage of the Japanese Yen's relative strength, with the yen's value weakening against the US Dollar amid hawkish Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) minutes. This move was also influenced by the Euro's weakness, which led to a capitalization of the Yen's value. As a result, the USD/JPY pair edged higher in the 158-yen range, driven by the yen's downside risks near 158.50, according to MUFG.

brief:
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq rose to new highs, driven by a rebound in tech stocks, while the 10-year yield rose 0.29% amid concerns about market volatility.

S&P 500 (+0.54% to 7807.01): Tech Stocks Drive S&P 500 to New High. Traders are watching the tech sector's recovery, which boosted the S&P 500 to a record close. [1] [2] [4] The rebound in tech stocks is seen as a positive sign for the overall market. [3]
Nasdaq (+0.54% to 27340.99): Nasdaq Rebounds from AI Stock Sell-Off. The Nasdaq rose 0.54% after a report on OpenAI's revenue, which rattled AI stocks [5]. This move was also influenced by a rebound in tech shares following a recent sell-off [6]. Additionally, the Nasdaq's gain was partly driven by a decline in oil prices, which boosted the market's overall sentiment [4].
10-Year Yield (+0.29% to 5.25): Yield Hike Sparks Market Concerns. The 10-year yield rose 0.29% to 5.25% as traders weighed the implications of Pimco's warning that US Treasury yields risk hitting 6% for the first time since 2000. Investors are also watching the upcoming 30-year bond auction, with some expecting further hikes. The recent sell-off in global bonds has pushed US Treasury yields to fresh 24-year highs, sparking concerns about market volatility.
USD/JPY (+0.14% to 158.29): USD/JPY Rises on Yen Strength. The USD/JPY pair rose as traders took advantage of the Japanese Yen's relative strength, with the yen's value weakening against the US Dollar amid hawkish Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) minutes. This move was also influenced by the Euro's weakness, which led to a capitalization of the Yen's value. As a result, the USD/JPY pair edged higher in the 158-yen range, driven by the yen's downside risks near 158.50, according to MUFG.
Crude Oil (-0.3% to 91.22): Oil Prices Fall Amid Trump's Iran Comments. Oil prices fell as Trump paused talks of renewed strikes on Iran, which had caused a surge in prices. This move likely eased concerns among traders, who had been watching the situation closely. The decline in oil prices also contributed to a fall in stock futures, as seen in the early morning trading session [16].
Gold (+1.43% to 4216.5): Gold Prices Rise Amid Easing Yields. Gold prices rose as Treasury yields eased from 24-year highs, causing the dollar to pause, which made gold more attractive as a safe-haven asset [20]. This move was also influenced by the views of Peter Schiff, who sees rising yields as a bullish sign for gold [23]. Traders are watching the Fed's risk, particularly for December, which could impact gold prices [22, 23].

Also worth knowing:
- The Nasdaq led the Dow after surprise economic data, with Nutanix nearing a buy point.
- Trump has established a committee to investigate Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, amid efforts to fire her.
- Trump has launched a probe into Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, amid efforts to fire her.
